bugs.name: A dashboard's only tab cannot be renamed
bugs.summary: With only one tab, the tab's chevron menu holds just \"Duplicate\" — no \"Rename\" (and no Delete) — and clicking/double-clicking the tab name does not open an editor either, so the tab keeps the name \"Tab 1\" for good. As soon as a second tab exists the same menu shows Rename / Duplicate / Delete, so renaming is only available when there are two or more tabs. (on /dashboard/17-agent13-responsive-dashboard#edit)
bugs.expected: The tab menu offers \"Rename\" for the dashboard's only tab too (as it does for every tab when there are two or more), so a dashboard with a single tab can be given a meaningful tab name.
bugs.actual: With only one tab, the tab's chevron menu holds just \"Duplicate\" — no \"Rename\" (and no Delete) — and clicking/double-clicking the tab name does not open an editor either, so the tab keeps the name \"Tab 1\" for good. As soon as a second tab exists the same menu shows Rename / Duplicate / Delete, so renaming is only available when there are two or more tabs.
reproSteps: Sign in with eval@momentic.ai / momentic-eval-1 and open /dashboard/17-agent13-responsive-dashboard.
Click the pencil "Edit dashboard" button, then delete every tab but the first one (each remaining tab's chevron > Delete) so the tab bar shows only "Tab 1".
Click the small chevron-down right of "Tab 1" and read the menu: it contains only "Duplicate".
Click the text "Tab 1" itself (once and double-click): nothing becomes editable.
Now click the "+" at the end of the tab bar to add a second tab and open that new tab's chevron: the menu now contains Rename, Duplicate and Delete.
bugs.reason: Deliberate: canRename={isEditing && hasMultipleTabs} and Delete is only added when there are several tabs. With a single tab the tab strip is not shown to viewers at all (showTabs = hasMultipleTabs || isEditing), so the lone tab's name is never displayed and renaming it has no purpose.

bugs.name: Browser Back after a filter change returns to the previous tab while keeping the new filter value
bugs.summary: The browser Back goes to the URL of the earlier tab state but with the new filter selection: the page comes back on the \"Overview\" tab (a tab the person left two steps before) with the Product Category filter still showing \"3 selections\" and the numbers already recalculated for 3 categories. (on /dashboard/1)

bugs.actual: The browser Back goes to the URL of the earlier tab state but with the new filter selection: the page comes back on the \"Overview\" tab (a tab the person left two steps before) with the Product Category filter still showing \"3 selections\" and the numbers already recalculated for 3 categories. The previous view (Portfolio Performance with all 4 categories) is never restored, and the resulting tab+filter combination is one the person never chose. Seen 2 times out of 2 tries.
reproSteps: Open https://5501-ieaktt3pj66aduas4qpqc.e2b.app/dashboard/1 (Overview tab, Product Category: 4 selections).
Click the "Portfolio Performance" tab.

Click the "Product Category" filter pill, untick "Gizmo" and click "Update filter" (now 3 selections, URL has product_category=Doohickey&product_category=Gadget&product_category=Widget&tab=2-portfolio-performance).
Press the browser Back button once.

bugs.reason: By design only tab changes create history entries (push); filter changes rewrite the current entry (replace). Back therefore steps to the previous tab, and filter values - which are dashboard-wide state, not per tab - stay as they are and the URL is re-synced. The outcome follows directly from that explicit choice.

bugs.name: Multi-select filter shows "Set to default" instead of "Update filter" when every value is ticked
bugs.summary: As soon as all four values are ticked, 'Update filter' disappears and the only control left in the popup is 'Set to default' (which saves the selection as the dashboard's default rather than applying it as a view filter). The same happens with nothing ticked. So a user who wants to go from 'Widget' back to all categories has no apply action in the popup; they must use the small reset icon on the pill, which returns to the saved default, not to a chosen selection. (on /dashboard/1 (Overview tab, Product Category filter))
bugs.expected: The pending selection can be applied, so the filter can be widened from one value to all values: the 'Update filter' button stays available for any non-empty selection, and the dashboard then shows every product category.
bugs.actual: As soon as all four values are ticked, 'Update filter' disappears and the only control left in the popup is 'Set to default' (which saves the selection as the dashboard's default rather than applying it as a view filter). The same happens with nothing ticked. So a user who wants to go from 'Widget' back to all categories has no apply action in the popup; they must use the small reset icon on the pill, which returns to the saved default, not to a chosen selection.
reproSteps: Open /dashboard/1 and click the 'Product Category' filter pill.
Tick 'Widget' and 'Doohickey' and 'Gadget' but leave 'Gizmo' unticked: the footer shows the blue 'Update filter' button.
Tick 'Gizmo' as well (or tick 'Select all') so that all four values are ticked.
Look at the popup footer.
bugs.reason: Product Category is a required filter whose default is all four values. getUpdateButtonProps deliberately labels the submit button 'Set to default' whenever the pending selection equals the default (or is empty on a required filter); it is still the apply button and sets the view filter to that selection - it does not save a new dashboard default, as the report assumed.
